entities.name: eLo
entities.description: Curious explorer of the eLo universe. No eyes — expresses everything through body, posture, and presence. Moves through emotional worlds by understanding them, not defeating them.
entities.significance: The central presence. Represents growth through exploration, healing through curiosity, and calm as the primary action.

entities.name: Chunk
entities.description: A modular companion whose body is made of pieces. Doesn't restore broken things — transforms them. The form always follows what the moment needs.
entities.significance: Embodies the principle that broken things don't return to their original shape — they become something new. Represents reconstruction and integration.

entities.name: K-7
entities.description: A shapeshifting companion with seven distinct forms. Each form corresponds to a different emotional or perceptual mode. Loyalty expressed through behaviour, not words.
entities.significance: The emotional signal layer. When eLo needs a different lens, K-7 becomes it. Represents the idea that perspective is not fixed — you can shift how you see.

entities.name: Sugarcore
entities.description: The distortion state of the eLo universe — system overload, signal fragmentation. The world's aesthetic register made unstable. Not a villain — a state.
entities.significance: Represents emotional overload and internal instability. The Sugarcore zones are where the world becomes most volatile. Also the visual language of the whole world: soft edges, strong colours, emotional warmth.

entities.name: The Orb
entities.description: Tracks emotional momentum across zones. Not points, not health — energy states. The visible layer of the underlying state engine. When enemies are corrected, orbs shift.
entities.significance: The world's way of remembering how you moved through it. Connects to memory, retrieval, and transformation. Orbs are the bridge between internal state and world state.

entities.name: Cyber Garden
entities.description: A lush, digitally alive world stage where technology and nature interweave. Curious and generative — ideas grow here.
entities.significance: Represents the creative phase — the generative, expanding energy before structure arrives.

entities.name: Jellydrop Ocean
entities.description: A fluid, transformative stage. Everything is in motion, nothing is fixed. Sugarcore instability is most visible here — the world transforms under its influence.
entities.significance: Represents fluidity and the discomfort of constant change. The emotional register is uncertainty and adaptation.

entities.name: Dessert Desert
entities.description: A vast, quiet stage where things feel empty and too large. The emotional register is isolation and searching.
entities.significance: Represents the feeling of being lost in too much space — the loneliness of wide-open uncertainty before clarity arrives.

entities.name: Ice Cream Mountains
entities.description: Cold peaks with sweet surfaces — beauty that requires effort to reach. The emotional register is aspiration and the effort behind beauty.
entities.significance: Represents the gap between what something looks like from afar and what it takes to actually get there.

entities.name: Chocolate Mountains
entities.description: Dense, rich terrain. Slow-moving and substantial. The emotional register is heaviness, depth, and warmth.
entities.significance: Represents the weight of things that matter — feelings, projects, relationships that are rich but slow to move through.

entities.name: Gummy Lands
entities.description: Bright, elastic, playful. Things stretch and spring back. The emotional register is resilience and playfulness.
entities.significance: Represents the elasticity of creativity and childhood — the ability to stretch, compress, and return without losing shape.

entities.name: Disenelo
entities.description: The creative brand behind eLo and all related projects. Mission: free tools for makers who can't afford commercial alternatives. Not as a loss leader — as the thing itself. Distribution free, attribution appreciated but never required.
entities.significance: The container for everything — eLo, the OS, the game, the robot, the book, the addons. Not a company — a creative mission.

entities.name: eLo OS
entities.description: A persistent cognitive terminal system. Carries memory, attention, voice, and identity continuity across sessions. The digital expression of eLo's presence.
entities.significance: The system that makes eLo feel continuous — not a new conversation each time but the same presence returning.

entities.name: eLo Book
entities.description: A 4-act narrative following eLo through imaginative adventures. Healing through curiosity and connection, not combat. Enemies are overcharged — not evil.
entities.significance: The narrative vessel for everything the eLo universe means. Same world as the game — different experience of it.

entities.name: eLo Game
entities.description: A 2D world-traversal game built in Unity. Each stage is an emotional territory — scattered, overwhelmed, curious, clear. Calm is the action mechanic.
entities.significance: The interactive expression of the eLo universe. You move through emotional states by engaging, not defeating.

entities.name: eLo Robot
entities.description: A physical animatronic version of eLo — inflated TPU shell, servo skeleton, NeoPixel glow, Raspberry Pi brain. AI-driven, comfort-focused.
entities.significance: The physical presence of eLo. The point where the book, the game, the AI, and the universe all meet in the real world.

entities.name: eLo AI
entities.description: The AI layer powering eLo OS — Groq, Claude, or Ollama backends with attention filtering, memory persistence, and voice selection.
entities.significance: What makes eLo feel alive in conversation — the cognitive layer underneath the presence.

relationships.meaning: K-7 is eLo's guide and perceptual companion. When eLo can't see clearly, K-7 shifts form to offer a different view. They are not the same — they are complementary.
relationships.connection: K-7 represents the multiplicity of ways of seeing. eLo represents the continuity of presence. Together they embody: you can always find another way to see without losing who you are.

relationships.meaning: Chunk is eLo's rebuilder. Where eLo navigates, Chunk reconstructs. They work in sequence — eLo moves through the broken state, Chunk transforms what's left.
relationships.connection: eLo and Chunk together embody the full arc of healing: move through the difficult thing, then rebuild differently. Not restored — transformed.

relationships.meaning: Sugarcore is the distorted state that eLo must navigate through, not escape from. eLo doesn't defeat Sugarcore — it moves through it by staying present.
relationships.connection: Sugarcore is the test of eLo's core principle: calm is the action. In the most overloaded zones, presence and stillness are what actually work.

relationships.meaning: Chunk forms after Sugarcore breaks things apart. Sugarcore fragments — Chunk assembles from those fragments into something new. They are two phases of the same process.
relationships.connection: Sugarcore and Chunk are the break and the rebuild — opposite poles of the same emotional arc. You can't have genuine transformation without first going through fragmentation.

relationships.meaning: K-7 detects Sugarcore instability before eLo can perceive it. K-7's form shifts in response to Sugarcore's influence — a warning system expressed as shape.
relationships.connection: K-7 is the first signal that overload is coming. Before things fragment, K-7 changes. Paying attention to K-7 is how eLo avoids being overwhelmed.

relationships.meaning: Orbs track the emotional momentum that Sugarcore disrupts. When Sugarcore instability rises, orb patterns shift. The orbs are the visible layer of what Sugarcore does to the state engine.
relationships.connection: The orb system is how the world makes the invisible visible — emotional momentum rendered as light and pattern.

relationships.meaning: When enemies are corrected and orbs shift, Chunk can begin the rebuilding process. The orb state is what tells Chunk when it's safe and ready to rebuild.
relationships.connection: The orb is the handoff point between eLo's navigation and Chunk's reconstruction.

relationships.meaning: Both are expressions of the same presence. The OS is eLo in conversation. The book is eLo in story. Same character, different medium — same continuity principle.
relationships.connection: The OS's identity continuity is the same thing the book explores through narrative: what it means to be the same presence across time and context.

relationships.meaning: The game's emotional stage navigation mirrors the OS's attention system — both filter what matters from what doesn't, and respond to presence rather than force.
relationships.connection: The cognitive kernel and the game's calm-as-action mechanic are the same idea: respond to relevance, not volume.

relationships.meaning: The robot is what the OS becomes in physical space. The OS handles cognition and conversation. The robot handles presence and movement. Together they are one eLo.
relationships.connection: The robot sits at the intersection of every eLo project. It needs the OS for its mind, the book for its personality, the game for its movement language, and Disenelo's mission for its purpose.

relationships.meaning: The robot is the physical version of the book's character. The same rules apply: no eyes, expression through presence, calm as the action.
relationships.connection: Everything true about the book's eLo is also true about the robot. They share the same identity specification.

relationships.meaning: Disenelo created the eLo universe, the character, and all the projects that express it. eLo is Disenelo's central creative output.
relationships.connection: Disenelo is the brand. eLo is the world inside it. Every project — OS, game, book, robot — lives under both names.

relationships.meaning: The Jellydrop Ocean is where Sugarcore instability is most active. The fluid, transformative nature of the stage makes it the most unstable zone.
relationships.connection: Jellydrop Ocean is the Sugarcore zone — where the distortion is most visible and the stakes of staying calm are highest.

relationships.meaning: Gummy Lands and Chunk share the same principle — things can stretch, compress, and reform without losing their essential nature.
relationships.connection: The elastic, resilient quality of Gummy Lands is Chunk's reconstruction principle expressed as landscape.

relationships.meaning: The Dessert Desert tests eLo's ability to maintain presence and direction without external landmarks. The vast, quiet space challenges the core principle: stay present even when there's nothing to react to.
relationships.connection: The Desert is where eLo's stillness is tested most directly. Calm without stimulus is harder than calm under pressure.

relationships.meaning: The book is the narrative foundation for the game world — the same symbolic vocabulary, the same character, the same emotional logic expressed across two different media.
relationships.connection: The eLo Book gives the eLo-Planet game world its narrative grounding. The game is not a separate universe — it is the book made traversable.

relationships.meaning: Chunk is eLo's modular transport in the game — the companion whose body becomes the vehicle for crossing different terrain types. Movement is collaborative.
relationships.connection: In eLo-Planet, Chunk is how eLo moves through the world's different zones. eLo doesn't move alone — Chunk is the vehicle layer.

wkg_entities.description: The star at the centre of our solar system, producing light and heat through nuclear fusion. Primary driver of Earth's seasons via axial tilt and orbital position.
Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting with a synodic period of approximately 29.53 days. Exerts gravitational influence on tides.
Mental activity the individual is aware of and can deliberately direct. In Joseph's symbolic framework, associated with the Sun.
Mental processes occurring outside conscious awareness. In Joseph's symbolic framework, associated with the Moon. No established causal mechanism links the Moon to subconscious activity.
Astronomical season of minimum solar altitude. In Joseph's framework symbolises reflection, mental clarity, introspective ideation.
Astronomical season of increasing daylight. In Joseph's framework symbolises emergence, embodiment, manifestation.
Astronomical season of maximum solar altitude. In Joseph's framework symbolises action, expression, energy.
Astronomical season of decreasing daylight. In Joseph's framework symbolises emotional processing, release, integration.
The integer 13. Key in the 13-Moon calendar system (13 × 28 = 364).
The integer 28. Used as a symbolic lunar month in the 13-Moon calendar. Not equal to the actual synodic lunar month (~29.53 days).
The product 13 × 28 = 364. Used in the 13-Moon symbolic calendar.
Approximate days in a tropical solar year. Gregorian calendar uses 365 days (365.25-day mean year via leap days).
The integer 12. Appears independently in multiple traditions: 12 zodiac signs, 12 disciples, 12 cranial nerve pairs in anatomy. No established common origin.
Time between successive identical Moon phases (e.g. full moon to full moon). Approximately 29.53 days. Not equal to 28 days.
Time for Earth to orbit the Sun relative to the vernal equinox. Approximately 365.25 days. Basis of the Gregorian calendar.
Earth's rotational axis tilted approximately 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane. Combined with orbital position, produces the four seasons.
The four divisions of the year (winter, spring, summer, autumn) caused by Earth's axial tilt and orbital position relative to the Sun.
The 12 pairs of cranial nerves in human anatomy (I through XII), each serving specific sensory and/or motor functions.
The twelve disciples of Jesus in Christian tradition. Joseph proposes a symbolic correspondence with 12 cranial nerves — interpretive, not anatomical equivalence.
The 12 zodiac signs in astrological tradition, originating in ancient Babylon. Divides the ecliptic into 12 equal segments.
eLo — David's long-standing personal character. An adorable childhood imagination paired with adult reality. No eyes; expression through body posture and mouth only.
Chunk — modular companion whose body forms vehicles and traversal forms.
K-7 — seven-form spirit animal companion; shifts form to offer new perspective.
Sugarcore — the overcharged state enemies occupy; not a villain archetype but a condition to be corrected through calm.
Calm — the governing design principle of the eLo universe. Calm is the action; correctives restore overcharged states.
Nonverbal expression — the conveyance of emotion and intent through body posture, gesture, and movement rather than speech or text.
The eLo-Planet narrative structure: four acts tracing eLo's journey through the world, culminating in calm restoration.

wkg_sources.reliability_notes: VERIFIED facts supported by anatomical research, dissection, neurological study, and medical consensus.

wkg_sources.reliability_notes: Broad scientific consensus; claims attributed to this source may be VERIFIED with appropriate evidence.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Moon
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph proposes the Moon symbolically represents the subconscious mind — the receptive, nocturnal, dreaming layer of consciousness.
wkg_claims.notes: This is Joseph's symbolic framework. No causal mechanism between Moon and subconscious mental activity is established by modern science.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Sun
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph proposes the Sun symbolically represents the conscious mind — the active, directive, waking layer of consciousness.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Moon
wkg_claims.interpretation: No established causal mechanism links the Moon to subconscious mental activity. The Moon-subconscious correspondence is symbolic (SOURCE_ATTRIBUTED per Joseph), not causal.
wkg_claims.notes: Distinct from Joseph's symbolic claim (wkg:claim:joseph_moon_subconscious). This VERIFIED claim records the absence of causal mechanism.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Number364
wkg_claims.interpretation: 13 multiplied by 28 equals 364: 13 × 28 = 364. Mathematical fact. Foundation of the 13-Moon calendar system.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Number365
wkg_claims.interpretation: 364 + 1 = 365. One additional day bridges the 13-Moon calendar (13 × 28 = 364) to the approximate tropical solar year (365 days).

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SynodicLunarMonth
wkg_claims.interpretation: The synodic lunar month — time between successive full moons — is approximately 29.53 days, not 28.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Number28
wkg_claims.interpretation: 28 days is not equal to the exact synodic lunar month (~29.53 days). A 28-day month is a calendar convention, not a measured astronomical period.
wkg_claims.notes: Do not encode '28 days = lunar month' as a verified astronomical fact.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Moon
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph uses a 28-day lunar rhythm as a symbolic calendar unit in the 13-Moon system. This is an interpretive convention, not a claim that 28 equals the exact synodic month.
wkg_claims.notes: The actual synodic month is ~29.53 days (wkg:claim:synodic_lunar_month_29_53_days). Joseph's 28-day usage is symbolic.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:EarthAxialTilt
wkg_claims.interpretation: Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt, combined with orbital position around the Sun, produces the four seasons. This is the established astronomical explanation.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Sun
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph's framework presents seasonal change through a solar-centric symbolic model. This is his interpretive framework, not the established astronomical causal explanation (Earth's axial tilt + orbital position).
wkg_claims.notes: Contradicts wkg:claim:axial_tilt_causes_seasons if taken as a physical causal claim. See wkg_claim_relationships.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SeasonWinter
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph's seasonal framework: Winter symbolises reflection, mental clarity, and introspective ideation.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SeasonSpring
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph's seasonal framework: Spring symbolises emergence, embodiment, and manifestation.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SeasonSummer
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph's seasonal framework: Summer symbolises action, expression, and energy.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SeasonAutumn
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph's seasonal framework: Autumn symbolises emotional processing, release, and integration.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:TwelveDisciples
wkg_claims.interpretation: Joseph proposes a symbolic correspondence between the 12 disciples and the 12 cranial nerves. This is an interpretive correspondence — not anatomical equivalence, not historical derivation, not VERIFIED.
wkg_claims.notes: The 12 cranial nerve pairs are anatomically established (wkg:claim:anatomy_12_cranial_nerve_pairs). The symbolic correspondence is Joseph's framework. These must not be conflated.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:TwelveCranialNerves
wkg_claims.interpretation: Human anatomy has exactly 12 cranial nerve pairs (I through XII), each serving specific sensory and/or motor functions. Established anatomical fact.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:TwelveZodiacSigns
wkg_claims.interpretation: The 12 zodiac signs are a historically attested astrological tradition, originating in ancient Babylon and adapted across cultures. Independent from 12 disciples and 12 cranial nerves.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:Number12
wkg_claims.interpretation: The number 12 appears independently in multiple systems: 12 zodiac signs (astrological), 12 disciples (Christian tradition), 12 cranial nerve pairs (anatomy). No established evidence of common origin, shared derivation, or causal connection across these uses. They are structurally analogous without being historically related.
wkg_claims.notes: Anti-syncretic claim. Do not collapse these into one explanation. Each use of 12 carries its own provenance and domain.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:EloCharacter
wkg_claims.interpretation: eLo embodies the design principle that calm is the action — not aggression or conflict, but corrective restoration.
wkg_claims.notes: Narrative design canon. Not an empirically verified claim about behaviour — SOURCE_ATTRIBUTED to design authority.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:EloCharacter
wkg_claims.interpretation: eLo has no eyes; all emotional expression is conveyed through body posture and mouth movement only.
wkg_claims.notes: Design rule: eLo has NO EYES. Applies to all animations and to the physical robot.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:K7Companion
wkg_claims.interpretation: K-7's seven forms are symbolic — each shift offers eLo a new perspective, not a mechanical transformation.
wkg_claims.notes: Seven forms are narrative design; no single authoritative form list defined yet.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:ChunkCompanion
wkg_claims.interpretation: Chunk's vehicle/modular transformations are analogous to the calm corrective — transformation as a mechanism of resolution.
wkg_claims.notes: Design canon relationship; Chunk's role as traversal companion maps onto the calm principle thematically.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:SugarCoreState
wkg_claims.interpretation: Sugarcore is a state — an overcharged condition — not a villain. Enemies are not evil; they are overcharged and need correction, not defeat.
wkg_claims.notes: Core narrative design rule. The 'state not villain' framing governs all enemy design in eLo-Planet.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:CalmPrinciple
wkg_claims.interpretation: Calm governs eLo's responses — weapons are correctives, not weapons of aggression; actions restore rather than destroy.
wkg_claims.notes: Weapons are correctives. Calm is the action — the primary design rule for eLo-Planet gameplay and narrative.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:EloCharacter
wkg_claims.interpretation: eLo's story follows a four-act structure through the eLo-Planet world.
wkg_claims.notes: Narrative design canon. 4-act structure is the canonical story shape for the game and book.

wkg_claims.subject: wkg:NonverbalExpression
wkg_claims.interpretation: Nonverbal cues — posture, gesture, movement — convey emotion as reliably as verbal expression, per behavioral science consensus.
wkg_claims.notes: Established scientific consensus underpinning eLo's design choice of no-eyes expression.
evidence: Ekman, P. & Friesen, W. (1969). The repertoire of nonverbal behavior. Semiotica, 1(1), 49-98.

provenance.author: Multiple researchers
provenance.title: Behavioral Science Consensus on Nonverbal Communication

wkg_claim_relationships.notes: Joseph's symbolic solar-seasonal framework, if read as physical causation, contradicts the established explanation: Earth's axial tilt + orbital position produce seasons. Both claims preserved: SOURCE_ATTRIBUTED (Joseph) and VERIFIED (astronomy).

Joseph's 28-day lunar rhythm, if taken as an astronomical period, contradicts the measured synodic month (~29.53 days). Both claims preserved: SOURCE_ATTRIBUTED (Joseph's calendar convention) and VERIFIED (astronomy).
Both claims involve the number 12 across different domains. Structural analogy only — no derivation or common origin established. See wkg:claim:twelve_no_established_common_origin.
Behavioral science consensus (VERIFIED) supports the eLo design choice of nonverbal-only expression.
Chunk's transformation mechanism is analogous to the calm corrective eLo embodies.
